subject.title: [Feature]: Add OpenClaw Settings chat on iOS and Android

question: Should OpenClaw ship dedicated privileged Settings → OpenClaw chat destinations in both native mobile apps, with the issue’s proposed `openclaw.chat`-only contract and two-PR delivery plan?
rationale: This is a new user-facing, privileged mobile capability rather than a repair of established behavior; the existing prerequisite intentionally separates system agents from ordinary selectors but does not choose this Settings UX or its operator-security posture.

options.title: Sponsor the two-PR mobile plan
options.body: Confirm the dedicated Settings destination and require independently proven iOS-first and Android-second implementations against the existing Gateway contract.

options.title: Narrow to one mobile platform first
options.body: Select iOS or Android as a product pilot before committing to matched behavior across both native clients.

options.title: Defer native parity
options.body: Keep macOS and Control UI as the supported system-agent administration surfaces until mobile privileged-chat requirements are prioritized.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the two-PR mobile plan
recommendation.body: Confirm the dedicated Settings destination and require independently proven iOS-first and Android-second implementations against the existing Gateway contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The related merged protocol work and this detailed mobile proposal make steipete the clearest available routing candidate for the product-boundary decision.
